chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Salih ibn 'Uqbah, from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, who said:

I asked Abā 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him), 'What is [the reward] for one who visits the grave of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)?' He replied, '[It is] like one who visits Allah on His Throne.'

key_terms.زَارَ: To visit (a shrine or grave for spiritual benefit)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting the grave of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him) states that the reward for visiting the grave of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) is equivalent to the reward of visiting Allah on His Throne, highlighting the high spiritual status of the Prophet's grave. This profound analogy, rooted in Shia hadith literature, underscores the concept of *ziyarah* as a means of drawing near to the Divine through the Prophet's presence, reflecting the belief that the grave of the Prophet serves as a spiritual axis connecting the earthly realm to the divine throne. The comparison elevates the act of visiting the Prophet's resting place to a near-direct encounter with God's majesty, emphasizing the unique ontological status of the Prophet in Shia theology.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 20. Muḥammad ibn Ja’far Al-Razzāz narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain, from Muḥammad ibn Ismā’īl, from Sāliḥ ibn ‘Uqbah, from Zayd Al-Shaḥḥām, who said:

I asked Abā ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)), “What is the reward for those who go to the Ziyārah of the grave of the Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.)?” Imam (a.s.) replied, “They are like those who perform the Ziyārah of Allāh on His Throne.”
